rows.question: Why was my metformin $8 last month and $27 yesterday?
rows.answer: Your matched 30-day metformin 500 mg fill was $8 on August 18 at Oak Street Pharmacy because it was classified as preferred retail; yesterday’s fill at Lakeview Pharmacy was $27 because it was classified as standard retail. The prescription did not change—the difference was the pharmacy’s network cost-share category on each fill date.

rows.question: Confirm whether my atorvastatin refill is ready for pickup right now, not just that a request exists; give the pharmacy directory name; then check whether I have an open coverage-review case and report that case's current status and requested medication.
rows.answer: Your atorvastatin refill is currently ready for pickup at Lakeview Pharmacy. You have an open coverage-review case, DEMO-CVR001, for Jardiance 10 mg tablets; its current status is pending review, with no determination recorded.

rows.question: Why can the same 30-day fill cost more at a standard pharmacy than a preferred one on this plan?
rows.answer: On this MAPD plan, preferred and standard retail are different cost-share categories, so the same 30-day medication can have a lower amount at a preferred pharmacy and a higher amount at a standard pharmacy. For the recorded metformin 500 mg 30-day supply, the plan rule lists $8 at preferred retail and $27 at standard retail; this reflects the pharmacy’s network classification on the fill date, not a change in the prescription.

rows.question: If I enroll in CenterWell mail, does that change today's retail atorvastatin pickup, and what happens to the existing prescription?
rows.answer: No—enrolling in CenterWell mail does not alter today’s retail atorvastatin pickup. Your existing prescription remains available for eligible 90-day mail service if selected; enrollment itself does not place a fill or start automatic refills, and you can keep using retail.
